title: The Companions of the Cave and Their Dog
summary: The story of faithful young men who took refuge in a cave, and Allah caused them to sleep for hundreds of years, accompanied by a dog guarding the cave's entrance. (QS. Al-Kahf: 9-26)
moral: Hold fast to your faith even when it is hard, and seek refuge with Allah. Allah protects His servants in ways we do not expect.
pages: Long ago, several young men believed in Allah in a city. The king and his people worshipped others besides Allah. The young men stood firm in their faith, and Allah increased their guidance.

Fearing they would be forced to abandon their faith, they went to a cave in the hills and prayed, 'Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and make our affair right for us.' (QS. Al-Kahf: 10). A dog followed them.
Allah caused them to sleep soundly in the cave for many years. Their dog lay with its two forelegs stretched out at the entrance of the cave, guarding as usual.
The sun rose and set each day. Its light shifted away from the cave so they would not be scorched. That was one of the signs of Allah's power, and they were kept safe under His protection.
Night turned to day, and the seasons changed: heat, rain, and cold snow. They slept for three hundred and nine years, and the dog stayed in its place.

Then Allah woke them. They asked one another, 'How long have we stayed here?' Some answered, 'Perhaps a day or part of a day.' Then they sent one of them to buy good food in the city with silver coins.

The people of the city finally learned what had happened, and they realised that Allah's promise is true and that the Day of Resurrection will surely come. From this story we learn to stand firm in faith and to trust in Allah's protection. The end.
